summary: EU, UK and ECOWAS citizens (among others) enter Cabo Verde visa-free, many other nationalities can obtain a tourist visa on arrival for about EUR 25, and since 1 January 2026 nationals of 91 listed countries need a visa from an embassy before travel, but every traveler must pre-register on the official EASE platform and pay the airport security tax before flying.

vaccinations.text: A yellow fever certificate is required only from travelers aged 1 year and over arriving from a country with risk of yellow fever transmission — not for direct arrivals from Europe or the Americas.

declarations.text: All international arrivals must pre-register their trip on the official EASE platform (ease.gov.cv) and pay the airport security tax before traveling — airlines check for it at check-in.

currencyLimits.text: Cash of EUR 10,000 or more (or the equivalent) must be declared on arrival and departure.

source.name: EASE — official Cabo Verde travel pre-registration platform

payments.text: Cards work in resort hotels, larger restaurants and supermarkets on Sal, Boa Vista and Santiago, but small guesthouses, taxis and markets want escudos. Euros are widely accepted in tourist areas. The escudo is pegged at about 110 to the euro.

safety.text: Canada advises a high degree of caution in Cabo Verde due to crime, which is higher on Santiago (especially Praia), Sal, Maio and Boa Vista. Pickpocketing and bag-snatching are frequent in crowded places such as markets in Praia and Mindelo, and violent crime, including armed robbery, occurs frequently at night and in isolated areas. Avoid deserted areas and hillside staircases after dark.

source.name: Government of Canada — Cabo Verde travel advice

bestTimeToVisit.text: November to April is dry and warm with steady trade winds — peak season for beaches, windsurfing and hiking on Santo Antão; August to October is more humid with occasional rain.

idp.text: Cabo Verde is a party to the 1968 Vienna Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1949 Geneva one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1968 Vienna version. A permit issued under the 1949 Geneva Convention carries no treaty obligation here.

source.name: UN Treaty Collection — Convention on Road Traffic (Vienna, 1968), status of parties
source.instrument: Convention on Road Traffic, Vienna, 8 November 1968 (UNTS vol. 1042, p. 17)

driving.text: Cabo Verde is a party to the 1968 Vienna Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1949 Geneva one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1968 Vienna version. A permit issued under the 1949 Geneva Convention carries no treaty obligation here. Whether a permit is required in addition to a national license, and for how long a foreign license may be used, are set by national road law and have not been checked for Cabo Verde yet.

source.name: UN Treaty Collection — Convention on Road Traffic (Vienna, 1968), status of parties
source.instrument: Convention on Road Traffic, Vienna, 8 November 1968 (UNTS vol. 1042, p. 17)

tips.text: Register on ease.gov.cv and pay the airport security tax before you fly — airlines check the confirmation at check-in, and doing it in advance skips a line on arrival.
Each island is distinct and connections take planning — internal flights and inter-island ferries sell out in season, and ferry schedules shift with the weather; book ahead.
Atlantic currents are strong and drownings happen every year off Santa Maria and Boa Vista — swim only at beaches locals recommend and heed flag warnings.
Euros are accepted almost everywhere tourists go, but change is given in escudos. Carry small notes and some CVE cash for markets and rural areas.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Cabo Verde?
faq.answer: EU, UK and several other European citizens enter visa-free for up to 30 days under the 2019 visa-waiver, and ECOWAS citizens enter freely. Many other nationalities, including US travelers who stay beyond the waiver arrangements, can obtain a tourist visa on arrival at international airports for about EUR 25. Since 1 January 2026, nationals of 91 countries on the government's list must get a visa from a Cabo Verde embassy before travel, including for transit. Everyone must pre-register on the EASE platform first.

faq.question: What is the EASE registration and the airport tax?
faq.answer: EASE (ease.gov.cv) is Cabo Verde's official pre-registration platform. Before flying, every international traveler registers their trip and pays the airport security tax (TSA) of 3,400 escudos — about EUR 31. Airlines check the confirmation at check-in.

faq.question: How long can EU citizens stay in Cabo Verde?
faq.answer: Up to 30 days visa-free under the EU–Cabo Verde arrangement in force since 2019. Longer stays require an extension from immigration in Cabo Verde or a visa from an embassy before travel.

faq.question: Do I need a yellow fever vaccine for Cabo Verde?
faq.answer: Only if you arrive from a country with risk of yellow fever transmission, such as much of mainland West Africa. Direct arrivals from Europe or the Americas do not need the certificate.

faq.question: Can I pay in euros in Cabo Verde?
faq.answer: Yes, in most tourist areas — hotels, restaurants and excursion operators widely accept euros at the fixed rate of roughly 110 escudos per euro. You will still want escudos for markets, taxis and the quieter islands.
